The smell of turpentine usually calmed Liam, but today it only heightened the nausea churning in his stomach. He stood before the canvas, brush hovering, but his eyes were fixed on the heavy oak door that separated his studio from the rest of the house. Inside, his father was likely reviewing the quarterly ledgers of the family’s construction firm, a business Liam had promised to inherit. The silence from the other side of the door was heavier than any shout.

Liam dipped his brush into a puddle of crimson, intending to paint the sunset he had witnessed that morning, but his hand trembled. He wasn't just painting; he was hiding. The easel was a barricade. He had spent the last three weeks secretly submitting his portfolio to the prestigious Art Institute in New York, a decision he had kept from his father to avoid the inevitable explosion. But the acceptance letter had arrived that morning, slipped under the door like a secret agent’s note. Now, the tension wasn't just about a career choice; it was about deception.

A floorboard creaked in the hallway. Liam froze, the brush dripping a single, violent drop of red onto the pristine white floorboards. The sound of his father’s footsteps grew louder, deliberate and heavy, approaching the studio door. Liam’s heart hammered against his ribs, a frantic rhythm that drowned out the quiet hum of the city outside. He had seconds to decide: hide the letter and lie, or face the man who had built his world and watch it crumble. The door handle began to turn.
